candidate_relations.reason: Sclerosing hemangioma is a vascular tumor (hemangioma variant) with fibrotic/sclerotic stroma, characterized by peripheral ring enhancement, high ADC values, and hypointensity on hepatobiliary phase MRI. Hepatocellular adenoma is a hepatocellular neoplasm with different imaging characteristics (arterial enhancement, iso/hyperintense on hepatobiliary phase in some subtypes, typically in young women on OCP). The imaging pattern here—peripheral ring enhancement, very high ADC values, FDG-negative, hypovascular on delayed phase—is consistent with sclerosing hemangioma, not adenoma. These are entirely different diagnostic entities.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Hepatocellular adenoma is a distinct benign hepatocellular neoplasm; sclerosing hemangioma is a vascular lesion with sclerotic change

case_quality_flags: High ADC values (mean 2.33×10^-3 mm^2/s) and FDG-negativity strongly support benign vascular etiology over adenoma
Sclerosing hemangioma is a rare diagnosis; absence of pooling on arteriography and peripheral ring enhancement are classic features
